entry.title: Kirby & The Amazing Mirror v0.5.0rc1
entry.content:
## v0.5.0-rc1
### New Features - Added eight Area Key progression items for Areas 2 through 9. Cross-area mirrors (and other transitions like Warp Stars) now require the destination area's key (Issue #42). - Add a default-on Area Keys option under Make the game easier. Turning it off removes Area Key requirements and replaces the eight keys with filler. - Added 15 Hub Connection progression items that unlock matching hub shortcuts while preserving alternate overland routes. Physical Big Switch checks remain independent, and received connections are restored across reconnects (Issue #482). - Add Hub Teleport Trap, which returns Kirby to Rainbow Route’s central hub (Issue #697). - Add `/goal` to display the seed's victory condition, including its resolved boss target while preserving legacy hidden targets (Issue #923). - Add Defeat a Number of Area Bosses: defeat any 1–8 distinct area bosses, default 3 (Issue #973). Other goals ignore the count. New count-goal seeds require the updated KirbyAM client; older clients interpret the new goal as Dark Mind.
### Improvements - None.
### Known Limitations - Only the North American ROM is supported; AP notifications are English. - Chests retain their original item sprites and collection animations; statues retain their original ability appearance. Mirrors and warp stars locked by Area Keys have no visual indicator. - mGBA notifications require the visible **Archipelago Connector** scripting panel; they are plain text, not game-image overlays.
### Bug Fixes - Avoid a misleading ROM compatibility warning when disconnecting from the server. - Resume item delivery and gameplay polling when continuing a completed save, while keeping ending, title and demo screens deferred (Issue #1004). - Keep duplicate incoming DeathLinks suppressed when reconnecting to the same seed and slot. - Preserve Mr. Frosty’s ice cubes and Boxy’s boxes as no-ability sources when passive-enemy ability randomization is disabled. - Keep Invincibility Candy queued until its native effect can start, including after leaving hubs or boss rooms and after an active Candy effect expires. - Honor excluded passive enemies, minibosses, and boss spawns in Completely Random ability mode. - Make repeated explicit `/toggle_text` disable commands safe for Kirby slots. - Recreate the mGBA connector listener after socket errors and ignore callbacks from an obsolete listener. - Keep Moonlight arrivals in Olive 6-13 behind the received Olive lever wall while preserving the physical RoomSanity check and return chute. - Retry mGBA connections after self-connected sockets or malformed VERSION replies instead of stopping the client. Shared Archipelago transport and the stock BizHawk launcher are unchanged. - Preserve excluded Minny grants in Completely Random mode while retaining normal ability gating (Issue #997). - Correct the Carrot Castle lever placement and labels to room 5-05 (Issue #972). - Restore outgoing DeathLink detection on dead gameplay frames while keeping fresh item delivery paused. Links received while already dead no longer kill the next respawn (Issue #975). - Restore packaged region discovery on Python 3.11 by using a package resource anchor. - Fix room-sanity generation by making each physical room check reachable from its valid compartment and restoring the missing Moonlight 2-05 lower descent (Issues #945, #969). - Random-per-room colors now update Kirby and the HUD when native palette transformations remain enabled during gameplay (Issue #966). - Allow the six guaranteed starting ability receipts and notices during the tutorial. Other items stay deferred, and Sword still requires its ability item (Issue #967). - Bootstrap Kirby build/test dependencies with checksum-pinned pip 26.2.2 and certifi 2026.10.19 after the eMudhra/emSign incident (Issue #978), with matching development guidance. Global AP dependencies, Docker and general workflows are unchanged.
### Internal Changes - Preserve compiled Hub switch mapping with generated lookup tables, fixed configuration addresses and explicit overlap checks. Historical native door aliases remain unchanged. - Verify the complete wheel inventory and SHA-256 bytes before offline Kirby ROM-smoke dependency installation (Issue #980; broader dependency matrices remain open). - Pin Kirby workflow actions to audited commit identities and reject mutable action references (Issue #981; interpreter/toolchain downloads remain separate). - Add draft-artifact receipts, signed provenance and download verification; refuse published-asset replacement (Issue #983). Plugin-trust guidance and owner immutability prerequisites are documented. - Gate Kirby publication on protected tags, release-environment approval and trusted-main validation; remove publisher PR authority and limit self-hosted smoke runs to main (Issue #982). - Carry the abandoned v0.4.2 security work into v0.5.0; see the [integration plan](https://github.com/hasherwi/Archipelago-kirbyam/blob/98ffe79fcef2e24690ec7d3fd7916cb07b1ef684/worlds/kirbyam/dev-docs/v050-security-integration.md) for dependencies and pending acceptance gates. - Execute the full native mailbox/ACK path for all 24 Spray Paint/Music Sheet IDs and Vitality grants for all four player structures, including duplicate delivery and dead-state safety (Issues #971, #953). - Exercise all eight shard receipts through twelve cold client/transport restarts, partial native saves and interleaved acknowledged food receipts (Issue #974). - Verify starting Vitality with stock-server empty/nonempty normal histories, duplicate precollects and repeated cold-RAM recovery without replay healing (Issue #943). - Integrate room connections and requirements into world-generation logic (PR #914).

entry.title: UZDoom v0.9.2
entry.content:
# 0.9.2
This is a bugfix release. There are new yaml options and tools for logic developers, but its main purpose is to fix several important bugs in 0.9.0 and 0.9.1 -- most notably an issue where combat logic often would not work at all.
⚠️ This version remains backwards compatible with 0.9.0 and 0.9.1, but since item categorization has changed, updating your logic packs (and rescanning any that you've made yourself) is recommended.
⚠️ New yaml options! Regen your templates.
🛈 [Logic pack downloads](../../blob/uzap-0.9.2/gzap/doc/support-table.md)
- New: - `ap_no_pool` category allows excluding items from the pool while still randomizing their locations. - Ashes 2063 logic updated to use `ap_no_pool` for the starting revolver. - All logic updated to use `ap_no_pool` for Allmaps. - Allmaps are now `medium` items for the purposes of location selection. - `progression_weapons_only` setting to include only logically required weapons in the pool. - For logic developers: - `spawn@tid` event type for spawn events targeting `MapSpots` and other TID-based spawns. (This doesn't really do anything you couldn't do before, but it makes it more convenient.) - Exiting a level normally (i.e. via an exit, not via the level select screen) will dump all regions in the level to the tuning file automatically. - Changed: - `medium` and `small` items now default to being unrandomized again, rather than shuffled. - `key` items are now always included in pretuning mode, since otherwise you can't pick them up at all. - Fixed: - "Invalid slot" error when using locally-generated PK3s and running the client without the `--slot` flag. - Doom 2 now has complete tuning for all items, thanks to Xindage. - Several problems with weapon logic either not working at all or not working properly. - Scanner crash when `cluster` directive is used. - Pretuning mode and, more generally, `vanilla` key placement no longer interacts badly with keys valid across multiple levels. - Hubclusters that appear in the middle of an episode (i.e. where the first map of the cluster is *not* the first map of the episode) are no longer unreachable from the level select screen. - Hitting a check inside a region, where your set of active keys includes keys not part of the region access requirements, now associates those keys with the check, making it possible to define locations that have more stringent access requirements than the regions that contain them. - `spawn` and `spawn@tid` EBLs targeting weapon types will now properly spawn a check when the weapon first appears, rather than waiting until the weapon locking subsystem thinks you're allowed to pick up the weapon.

entry.title: Homura-Hime v0.4.1
entry.content:
Feature release: the Soul Cores are items that gate the Chapter 6-8 boss fights, a new goal that only needs Chapters 6-8, optional locations as one setting, and options presets. See README for installation instructions.
**Update the plugin and the .apworld together and generate a new seed.** Seeds from 0.4.0 still play with this plugin, but they have no Soul Cores and no new goal. Two options of the YAML changed (see below): a YAML that names `encounter_clears` or `encounter_rewards` has to be edited.
### New:
**Soul Cores are items:**
- Each boss of Levels 1-5 leaves a Soul Core, and Chapters 6-8 fight the same five bosses again. The five Soul Cores (Agasa's, Ling Ling's, Chirakuin's, Yumiko & Kumiko's and Mamiya's) are now items of the multiworld, and the way to each rematch needs the core of that boss. - Without the core, the transition does nothing and the game says "<Name>'s Soul Core required to continue". This covers the doors to Ling Ling and the Corpse Princess, Nozomi, Yumiko & Kumiko's Demonic Realm and the Realm's own door, the walk to the memory tree before Agasa, and the pathway across the end of Chapter 8's last area before Mamiya. Everything else that leads to those fights (the Chapter Select, automatic changes of scene) is refused as well. - The hub used to hand the cores out when a world was cleared. Those five hand-overs are locations now ("Hub: Soul Core (1st World Cleared)" up to the 5th). The hub follows the number of worlds you have cleared, so the n-th core's location is checked after the n-th world you clear, whichever world that is. The cores are always shuffled, whatever `shuffle_key_items` says. - Shops show the Soul Cores with their own picture and description.
**Goal (`goal`: all_worlds / return_all_soul_cores):**
- `return_all_soul_cores` opens the Finale as soon as Chapters 6, 7 and 8 are cleared (which takes every Soul Core). Chapters 1-5 and the Climax stay playable for their checks but are not needed. It shortens the game when Chapters 6-8 can come before the other worlds: with a randomized order, or with freeform level keys. In the story order without freeform keys every world comes before Chapter 8 anyway. - The goal is still reported by the Kill ending, and a save has to have reached the Finale by the new rule.
**Optional locations (`optional_locations`, default on) replace `encounter_rewards`; `encounter_clears` is gone:**
- Every fight is a location now (110), always. Removed the toggle for removing mandatory fights as locations. - `optional_locations` decides whether the optional content counts: the ambush fights and their chests, the glitched-spirit trials, the Kushinada head chases and the optional fights (78 locations in all, the same ones `optional_location_importance` is about). Off: they are not locations, the game hands out what it always did there, and the fixed items they held leave the pool.
**Options presets:** Standard (the defaults), Balanced Random (balanced order, progressive keys, few traps) and Chaos (full random order, freeform keys, the Return All Soul Cores goal, most values random, Death Link on, cut content and advanced movement on).
**Packaging:** the .apworld is built with Archipelago's own "Build APWorlds" tool and keeps the tests out of the package; the world has a bug report page.
### Changes:
- The sample YAML is regenerated for this version.
### Known issues:
- Doing the Nurikabe's Hat quest shows the "found the hat" picture although the hat comes from the multiworld. Other quest items probably do the same. Undecided if I want to keep this behavior or not.

entry.title: Crash Team Racing v0.3.0a2
entry.content:
CTR Archipelago 0.3.0-alpha2 is up for testing! It fixes a lot of what you found in alpha1 and adds a few new things. It's still an alpha, so expect rough edges. **v0.2.4 stays the current stable release.**
[Full 0.3.0 notes on AP-Pie](https://ap-pie.com/ctr/releases/0-3-0) · [Setup guide](https://ap-pie.com/guides/ctr) · [SETUP.md as shipped](https://github.com/dowlle/ctr-native-ap/blob/v0.3.0-alpha2/SETUP.md)
## Before you try it
- **Use a new folder**, or replace your alpha1 folder. Your 0.2.4 install and rooms stay as they are. - **Use the alpha2 client and the alpha2 APWorld together.** An alpha1 room still connects to the alpha2 client. - **Make a new YAML** if yours is from 0.2.x. An alpha1 YAML still works, and there are a few new options.
## Fixed since alpha1
- Opening the tracker during the hub save camera could start a race with the save menu on screen. - Wumpa you get outside a race (shop or other players) is added right away. - Wumpa Wipeout removes all your fruit, also above 10. - Spoiler Items with coloured boxes off no longer stops the seed from starting. - Arcade, Time Trial, Versus and Battle play like the original game again. - Loading another save profile no longer keeps a racer that's locked in the room. - AP boxes on custom tracks no longer sink into the ground. - Cups and boss garages show the right track and racer names. - Hit Character checks count a boss race as soon as you can enter it. - Bosses on custom tracks no longer stall. - A boss cup now races the rival its garage names, and its banner reads "<Boss>'s Cup". - Only one Cortex Vortex per seed. - Custom track downloads retry on rate limits and show the real error. - Play Solo tells you which track it can't publish. - No more looping podium noise in the hub after a Trophy win.
## New
- **Custom Tracks screen:** Library, This Seed and Import tabs. The importer keeps track names, lets you rename them and imports all valid tracks at once. - **Custom track music:** custom tracks play their own music. - **Box Author Mode** in Options, Authoring: place and export AP boxes yourself. - **Play Solo:** every YAML option on the options screen, including lists like Crystal Arenas and the boss pools as checklists. The screen tells you when a value won't generate. No password by default, and no menu freeze with big libraries. - **Leaving a race pays:** Exit to map, Restart and a DeathLink loss bank the fruit you picked up, minus hits. Starting fruit never banks. - **Wumpa Shop pacing:** expensive shelves come into logic later, by Keys. New option `wumpa_shop_logic_scale`. - **Wumpa bundles** are on by default. - **Hint filters:** pad and shop hints can be limited to progression items, and pad hints can wait for Warp Pad Preview. - **Pad colours** match across the pad beam, hub map and tracker. Open pads have a green beam, stage 2 pads a blue-violet one, and a finished pad you can still replay for Wumpa keeps the light blue beam. - **Clearer YAML descriptions** for almost every option.
## Known issues
- The Custom Tracks screen still has rough edges: the Library can show only some of your tracks, the Project Saphi catalogue may not show, This Seed can say no seed is loaded while you're connected, and the Import help text is cut off. Fixes come in alpha3. - The race-start banner of a cup can show another cup's name, for example "Red Gem Cup" for the Purple Gem Cup. The standings show the right name. - Some menus are still hard to read where text runs over the logo. - A seed can still fail to generate with some unusual YAMLs. Generate again, and send me the YAML. - Short freezes can happen in some races. If you get one, tell me the track.
## Found a problem?
Post it in the [#ctr-bug-reports forum](https://discord.com/channels/522082434871722016/1567553276726091827) on Discord and say it's on 0.3.0-alpha2. Add your platform, YAML or seed, what happened, and the support bundle (`support-bundle.bat` on Windows, `support-bundle.sh` on Linux; look through it before you attach it). No Discord? [Open a GitHub issue](https://github.com/dowlle/ctr-native-ap/issues/new/choose) instead.
## Downloads
On Windows, grab `ctr-archipelago-v0.3.0-alpha2-windows-x86.zip`. On Linux or Steam Deck, grab `ctr-archipelago-v0.3.0-alpha2-linux-x86.tar.gz` (glibc 2.36 or newer). Each includes the client, the matching `ctr.apworld` and the Play Solo runtime. The separate `ctr.apworld` and `Crash.Team.Racing.yaml` are for hosts. You need your own NTSC-U disc; no game data is included. The client isn't code-signed.
The client is GPL-3.0; the source for this build is the `v0.3.0-alpha2` tag of this repository. Third-party licenses are in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `solo-runtime/LICENSES/` in each download.

## Pre-Release Version 0.4.0: In game unlock display **This is a version of the in game unlock display that does not require a new APWorld.** It is also a bit of a public test so please report any issues in the discord. There's some *known issues* with the mii's. Also for the vehicles screen there might be like a 0.5 seconds delay with the display updating, this is known please give it some time. entry.title: Kirby & The Amazing Mirror v0.5.0
entry.content:
## v0.5.0
The official v0.5.0 release of Kirby & The Amazing Mirror for Archipelago, built from main commit `744b1a5708ecaafd80313b7836a9197a25f5db0e`.
### Highlights - Eight **Area Keys** for Areas 2–9 gate cross-area travel. Locked mirrors show boards, associated Warp Stars stay hidden, and receiving a key updates eligible nearby routes while preserving other requirements. The default-on Area Keys option can be disabled to replace all eight keys with filler. - Fifteen **Hub Connections** unlock hub shortcuts independently of their physical Big Switch checks, while alternate overland routes remain available. - Eight new Kirby palettes: Rainbow, Candy Corn, Negative, Pineapple, Cotton Candy, Royal, Pumpkin and Mint Chip. - **Hub Teleport Trap**, the `/goal` command, and **Defeat a Number of Area Bosses** (1–8 distinct area bosses, default 3). New boss-count seeds require the updated KirbyAM client. - Fixes for lower-cave chest logic, Room Sanity reachability, starting-item delivery, DeathLink, reconnects, enemy ability randomization, Invincibility Candy and scaled enemy health.
### Why you may start with the Moonlight Mansion Area Key With Area Keys enabled, generation counts the checks your slot can actually reach with its starting inventory and the real access rules. If **fewer than four checks** are reachable, it gives you the **Moonlight Mansion - Area Key** at the start so you have more places to explore.
The key is moved out of the randomized item pool and its place is filled with a filler item, so this does not create a duplicate key or change the pool size. If at least four starting checks are reachable, generation does not automatically grant the key; it remains randomized unless you explicitly included it in your starting inventory.
**Room Sanity checks count toward that threshold.** With Room Sanity off, the corrected Rainbow Route 1-06 chest is no longer a free starting check, so the usual start receives the Moonlight Mansion key. With Room Sanity on, the additional reachable room checks can provide enough checks to keep the key randomized. Room Sanity is not a hard exemption: the same fewer-than-four rule applies to the actual starting state, including custom starting inventory. Disabling Area Keys disables this fallback.
### Downloads and verification files - **`kirbyam.apworld`** is the Archipelago world package to install. - **`kirbyam.provenance.json`** is a build receipt. It records the package's SHA-256 hash, source commit, tag, repository, workflow, and run/attempt so you can check that your download is the exact intended build. - **`kirbyam.attestation.jsonl`** is the signed GitHub build-provenance bundle for the APWorld and its receipt. It lets verification tools check that both files came from this repository's release workflow at the claimed source and tag, rather than trusting an unsigned checksum alone.
The two verification files are attached for integrity, provenance and auditing. They are not extra game content or files you install into Archipelago. Provenance verifies origin and bytes; it does not guarantee the absence of bugs. GitHub's automatically generated source archives are separate from these three release assets. No full ROMs or saves are included.
### Compatibility and details Only the North American ROM is supported. AP notifications are in English. Chests and statues retain their native item/ability appearance. mGBA notifications appear in the visible Archipelago Connector scripting panel, not over the game image.
See the [complete v0.5.0 changelog](https://github.com/hasherwi/Archipelago-kirbyam/blob/744b1a5708ecaafd80313b7836a9197a25f5db0e/worlds/kirbyam/CHANGELOG.md#v050), [save compatibility notes](https://github.com/hasherwi/Archipelago-kirbyam/blob/744b1a5708ecaafd80313b7836a9197a25f5db0e/worlds/kirbyam/dev-docs/rc4-file-selection-rollback.md), and [release verification guide](https://github.com/hasherwi/Archipelago-kirbyam/blob/744b1a5708ecaafd80313b7836a9197a25f5db0e/worlds/kirbyam/docs/release-preparation.md).

The **default for this setting was changed** to *30%* down from *50%*. - The **Starting Level Count** setting has been changed to go off of total check counts for your starting items. - Previously, it only added starting levels that were guaranteed to be completable to your max medal, and would not select any levels that don't have gifts. - This change was made to prevent restrictive starts even harder, and should make the start of the world more open. Thus, the **default for this setting was changed** to *3* down from *5*. Most settings couldn't reach 5 starting levels that fit in the criteria anyway. - New filler items have been introduced to help any potential filler feel less repetitive. - Added items: Garbage, Book of Death Page, Cloud 9 Minigolf Ball, Neon Mask, Secret of Heaven. - All of these are referenced in voiced dialogue! - (Hopefully with all of these changes, you won't be seeing that much of these anyway!)

entry.title: Castlevania - Aria of Sorrow v2026.11.1
entry.content:
- **New option: Progressive Movement.** Three Progressive Movement items replace Flying Armor, Malphas and Giant Bat, and always give them in that order. Your own copies show up as Skull Keys and need the client connected to grant their soul. - **Universal Tracker support.** UT now rebuilds your seed's logic from the server, with no YAML needed, including your logic difficulty and Hard Mode settings. Seeds generated before this release only give it their goal and Hard Mode setting, so it uses the defaults for their other logic options. UT also gets a map tab for the whole castle, the Chaotic Realm and each area, with a pin for every location colored by logic. It marks where Soma is and follows him from area to area, and nothing extra needs installing. Locations that only an out-of-logic trick reaches show in UT's color for reachable with tricks. - **New browser map tracker.** Type `/map` in the BizHawk Client or the Collection Client, or press their "Open map" button, to open a map of the castle in your browser. The Launcher also offers it as "Aria of Sorrow Tracker", including from a room page's link. It shows each location's logic status and where Soma is. By default it shows only the parts of the castle you have explored, which the Castle Maps reveal by area, and a toggle shows everything. Find Route draws the way from Soma's room to the location you select, except in race rooms. It runs on your own machine and needs nothing else installed. - **New option: Hard Mode Pickups.** The five Hard Mode-only pickups can be shuffled with Hard Mode (the default), always (they then spawn in normal mode too), or never. - **Giant Bat stays late.** With item smoothing on, the early mobility soul is now Malphas or Hippogryph, never Giant Bat. - **The Ancient Books explain themselves.** With Ancient Book Soul Drops on, Books 1 and 3 now say in the pause menu that their soul always drops. Book 2 has no drop effect, because the Giant Bat soul is a multiworld item, and the option text now says so. - **Clearer Advance Collection messages.** If the collection is running the Japanese or European Aria of Sorrow, Circle of the Moon or Harmony of Dissonance, the client now says which one and asks for the US Aria of Sorrow. - **Advance Collection installer:** it now asks where game.exe is if your Steam library isn't on the default path. If an install fails partway, it puts the collection's stock files back, and tells you if it couldn't. It now installs any seed, including ones generated for BizHawk, and the Launcher has a **CVAoS Collection Restore** button that puts the stock game back.
- **Renamed option:** "Library-to-Forbidden-Area Button Handling (Study Sealswitch)" is now **Forbidden Area Button**. Existing YAMLs still work, because the setting's name in the YAML (`forbidden_area_button`) is unchanged.
**Fixes** - Ability souls you receive (Malphas, Hippogryph, Galamoth and the rest) now arrive switched on. Before, they arrived switched off in the Ability menu and did nothing until you turned them on. - With Oops! All Whips on, logic no longer expects a weapon to break floors or ceilings, since every weapon swings like the Whip Sword. It waits for Black Panther instead. - With the Study Sealswitch shuffled, logic no longer expects you to climb from the Forbidden Area up to the Study without it. - Logic no longer counts on farming the Manticore that guards its room only once. - Seeds with the Study Sealswitch shuffled have a Lucky Charm again. The Sealswitch now takes the place of a 100 Gold pickup. - The room where the Forbidden Area button was no longer shows Castle Corridor's particle effects. - A DeathLink that arrives while Sky Fish is active now plays Soma's death animation. - A received item's "Got" box no longer replaces the box for something you picked up at the same moment. - Received weapons, armor and accessories now play the equipment pickup sound. - On a save made with the game's Copy option, received souls now count the ones you already had. Received gold now stops at the game's cap of 999,999. - The Collection Client now sends your checks again after it reconnects. - Starting inventory is now actually given to you in game, in seeds generated with this version. - Seeds already in progress keep working after you update. Their starting inventory still isn't given in game. - Item smoothing no longer puts progression in locations you excluded, takes it out of priority locations, or moves plando'd Ancient Books. - Seeds with many priority locations (about 25 or more) no longer fail to generate when item smoothing is on. - With Soul Shuffle and Keep Soul Drop Rates on, a Headhunter, Death, Legion or Balore soul that landed on an ordinary enemy could never drop. It now drops at that enemy's usual rate. - DeathLink deaths no longer pile up: one that arrives while Soma is already dead is dropped, and several during a pause kill him once. - Reconnecting while Soma is dying no longer sends his death to everyone a second time. - Moving on to a seed without DeathLink no longer leaves DeathLink switched on in the client. - A received item is no longer given twice when BizHawk pauses or the connection drops at the wrong moment. - Installing a different seed into the collection while the client is open now reconnects you as the new seed's slot. - The BizHawk client no longer stops working when a request times out, for example while BizHawk is paused. - Patching now checks that the base ROM is the original US ROM and says so if it isn't. - When the generator needs extra filler, it now makes only plain filler, never a soul or a Hard Mode item. - The Randomize Pickups option, which did nothing, is no longer shown.
**Installing** - Put `cvaos.apworld` in your Archipelago `custom_worlds` folder, replacing any older copy. It needs Archipelago 0.6.6 or newer. - Seeds from 2026.09.04 and 2026.10.30 still play with this version, so you can update partway through one. Seeds generated with this version need this version's clients, and older clients refuse them.

entry.title: Castlevania - Aria of Sorrow v2026.11.7
entry.content:
- **New Experimental options.** A collapsed "Experimental" group on the options page holds four new options and a new Soul Shuffle value. Their balance is measured but not play-tested, so they may change between versions. Each one is opt-in and off by default, so released YAMLs keep working and play as before. A Soul Shuffle of "random" still never picks the new value. The options page's "Experimental" preset turns all five on, at the settings they were measured with. - **Experimental: Enemy Checks.** The first defeat of each boss ("bosses", 10 checks) or of each kind of enemy ("all", 112 checks) is a check. The client reads defeats from the game's Enemy List, so one made while it is disconnected is sent when it reconnects. Each check adds one item from this game to the pool, and it is never progression. Iron Golem's and Final Guard's checks hold only filler for now. With "all" and the default hint cost, a hint costs 22 checks instead of 11. - **Enemy checks in hints, groups and trackers.** A hint for an enemy check names the rooms where that enemy appears. Location groups such as "Boss Defeats", "Unrouted Enemy Defeats" and "Chapel Defeats" let you exclude or prioritize enemy checks together. Both map trackers pin each check in every room where its enemy appears. - **Most enemy checks come late in logic.** The routes to most rooms' enemies aren't recorded yet, so logic expects all eight movement souls before those checks. You will usually make them much earlier, so once one of an enemy's rooms is reachable, the trackers show its check in their color for reachable with tricks. A boss's check needs only a way into its arena. - **Experimental: Soul Shuffle "matched".** Each soul trades places only with a soul of the same color and strength tier, rated from community tier lists. Each enemy keeps its own soul drop rate, so a run gives about as many souls of each color and tier as an unshuffled one. - **Experimental: Enemy Drop Rate.** Enemies drop their soul and their common item more often, from 100% (no change) up to 1000%. Enemies your seed reaches early get only a small part of the boost, while strong souls you could find early, rare drops and the better items keep their usual chance. Above 100, it replaces Multiply Soul Drop Rates. - **Experimental: Item Drop Shuffle.** The items that enemies drop move into the item pool, so any player's location can hold them. An enemy whose drop moved drops a similar item from this game instead. The drops are then dealt out again, so early enemies drop cheap items and the castle's last enemies drop the best ones. - **Experimental: Wide Item Smoothing.** Weapons and armor that are too good for the start of a run stay out of it, whether they come from a pickup, an enemy check, another world or an enemy drop. It also makes sure you hold an early weapon and armor, and it sets Item Smoothing to strict and Item Smoothing Order to spheres. In a multiworld it runs Archipelago's progression balancing itself, which a host can turn off with `wide_smoothing_runs_balancing` in host.yaml. - **New client commands: /souls and /drops.** In both clients, `/souls` lists which enemy drops each soul and how often, and `/drops` lists the items each enemy drops. They read the ROM you are playing, so they work for any seed. - **Drop tables in the spoiler.** When a seed changes which enemy drops which soul or item, or how often, the spoiler now lists every enemy's drops and their chances. - **Received gold gets its banner.** Gold you receive now shows the game's "$100"-style box and plays the gold sound, as a gold pickup does. - **Items have one name.** Every copy of an item now shares its plain name, so every Potion is "Potion" and a hint for "Potion" can find any of them. Location names still tell the pickups apart, and seeds from earlier versions still grant and track the same items. A YAML that names a numbered copy, such as "Potion (A)", still works in local and non-local items, start hints, item links' item pools and plando lists, where the old name now stands for every copy. In `start_inventory` and an item link's replacement item, use the plain name instead. - **Local play-data log.** The client now writes a log of each run to the `cvaos_play_data` folder inside your Archipelago `logs` folder. It records the souls you own, your checks, your equipped weapon and armor, and the drops your Enemy List shows. Nothing in it is sent to the server or to other players. - **Saves from another seed send no checks.** If you load a save that has received more items than the server has sent for this seed, such as one from another seed or a New Game+ started from one, the client holds back its checks and goal and prints a warning. It carries on once you load this seed's save. If the server lost its most recent checks in a crash, your own save can trip this too; type `/trust_save` to send its checks. - **New seeds need this version.** Seeds generated with this version need this apworld to apply their patch and this version's clients to play. An older apworld stops with "Unknown procedure", and an older client refuses the ROM. Seeds from the 2026.09.04, 2026.10.30 and 2026.11.01 releases still play with this version, so you can update partway through one. - **Patches that need a newer apworld say so.** From this version on, applying a patch that holds a feature this apworld doesn't know fails with a message naming the version the seed needs, instead of building a ROM without that feature. - **Cheaper filler.** When Archipelago needs extra filler for this game, as item links do, it now makes only cheap consumables and gold. Before, a linked player could get Gungner, Samurai Armor or other mid-game gear at the very start. It also stops adding a consumable you already have 9 of in your pool, the most the game lets you carry, and adds gold instead.
**Fixes** - Soma can now pick up a Skull Key while he holds 9. Before, a player who reached 9 Skull Keys while the client was disconnected could no longer collect other players' items. - When the Collection Client or the installer meets a seed it can't use, the message now names every patch format it accepts, rather than only the newest. - For contributors: the routing tool now builds the same graph as generation, a transdoor override that would change nothing fails at load, and an unusable custom pickup icon raises an error that names the problem instead of exiting.
**Installing** - Put `cvaos.apworld` in your Archipelago `custom_worlds` folder, replacing any older copy. It needs Archipelago 0.6.6 or newer. - Seeds from 2026.09.04, 2026.10.30 and 2026.11.01 still play with this version, so you can update partway through one. Seeds generated with this version need this version's apworld and clients.

entry.title: UZDoom v0.9.3
entry.content:
# 0.9.3
This is ostensibly a bugfix release, mostly focused on fixes to the rule compiler and combat logic.
However, it is also a feature release, and a big one, because this release finally adds support for
🔥🔥🔥 [**Hedon Bloodrite episode 1: Crystal Heart**](../../blob/uzap-0.9.3/gzap/wads/hedon_bloodrite/NOTES.md) 🔥🔥🔥
and Hedon support is something that has been a long-term goal of mine since I originally started this project nearly two years ago.
Episode 2 is likely going to be a while yet; it's both larger and more complicated than episode 1.
🛈 [Logic pack downloads](../../blob/uzap-0.9.3/gzap/doc/support-table.md)
- New: - Complete logic for Hedon Bloodrite episode 1 (MAP01-MAP10). - For logic developers: - An `AP-ITEM` record without a `pos` field will now define tag and category information for that item without adding any locations or items to the randomization pool. - New `overstock` flag allows configuring behaviour when items get pruned from the randomization pool. - `scanner { replacement ...; }` is now a valid construct that declares an actor replacement to be applied only when scanning, not when playing. - Fixed: - Generation should no longer fail if `AP-REGION` directives are re-ordered or if region access rules contain mutual recursion. - Another combat logic issue that would draw incorrect conclusions about reachability if weapons required by combat logic were not present in the pool. - Universal Tracker is now aware of which maps are starting maps (and thus have different combat logic behaviour in some configurations). - Per-map weapon mode no longer forgets about weapons that don't exist in some levels. - The inventory menu now respects `GZAPRC` `tag` directives for weapons. - `item/<name>/<count>` prereqs now work properly rather than always treating `count` as 1.
